summary: Closed T78#F-001 and T78#F-002, the two blockers the scope decision's single exception admits. F-001: the label path's cost no longer depends on any quantity the document writes. The `!` gate moved in front of the work it gates (the inline pass built reference constructs it never read); two necessary conditions were added, one of them structurally guaranteed (REFERENCE_DEF captures [^\]]+, so no key can ever contain `]`) which makes candidate spans pairwise disjoint and therefore linear in total; and a total-work budget of LABEL_WORK_FACTOR * content.length backstops the one filter a document can raise, flagging every definition rather than releasing anything when it is exhausted. Measured: T78's worst shape 20 802.7 ms -> 49.5 ms at 400 029 bytes, exponents 1.79/2.11/1.78 -> 1.14/0.91/0.84, all four public boundaries 1 948-2 278 ms -> 17.1-20.5 ms. With total bytes held constant at 262 144, sweeping the attacker's dials across five orders of magnitude moves the cost by 16.5 ms and 12.4 ms. F-002: the definition table keeps every definition of a label instead of the last, and every definition an image use resolves is flagged, which is correct under CommonMark's first-wins rule and under the opposite precedence; T78-dup leakingCount 6 -> 0. Sixteen prior matrices byte-identical, benign corpus unchanged at 16 files / 62 findings, suites 112/0/1168 exit 0, typecheck and eslint clean. No change to policies.md: this round makes an already-false sentence true and leaves every other one true.

artifacts.summary: The property the bound must have (P: no quantity the document writes changes the asymptotic cost), how it would be demonstrated, and the measured baseline. Written before any code.
What was changed, why each part of the bound is not inflatable, the full measurement tables before and after, the matrix hashes, the corpus explanation, and six concerns.

Ladders with growth exponents over fourteen adversarial shapes, the inflation table (bytes held constant while the attacker's dials are swept), the budget-exhaustion check, and the four boundaries on the worst shape.
One shape per process, so heap pressure from an earlier payload cannot be read as a cliff; used to settle whether the one exponent above 1.5 was real.
The four public boundaries across 128 KB to 1 MB for four shapes including a no-definition control and the budget-exhausting shape, best of three per cell.
Runs all nineteen prior matrix probes and hashes each output; invoked once before the change and once after.

changed_files.change: F-001: readBracketConstructs takes wantReference so the `!` gate precedes the work it gates; readLabel replaces labelWithinBudget and adds two necessary conditions (no key can contain `]`, and no key carries more `[` than the longest such run in the table) plus a total-work budget of LABEL_WORK_FACTOR * content.length whose exhaustion flags every definition; indexContent records `[` positions; lowerBound/countInRange added. F-002: the definition table's value is a list, every definition is kept, and every definition of a label an image use resolves is flagged. Header comment rewritten to state the property the bound has rather than the number it used to be.

Three tests added, all failing before the change: T81#F-002 (seven duplicate spellings including the reversed order, at the detector, through applyRedaction, the persistence materializer and the transport validator, with four controls); T81#F-001 perf (nineteen shapes, every one carrying a reference definition, under a 500 ms budget); T81#F-001 budget direction (a document that exhausts the work budget flags its definition and still honours the allowlist).
